content:
The [Calorie Calculator](/calorie-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Daily calories to maintain, lose or gain weight. Enter your sex, age, weight, height and activity level and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

This calorie calculator estimates your Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE) — the calories you burn each day — and the intake needed to lose or gain weight. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Health & Fitness tools include [BMI Calculator](/bmi-calculator), [BMR Calculator](/bmr-calculator) and [Body Fat Calculator](/body-fat-calculator).

## How to use the Calorie Calculator

Start by choosing your sex from the list, then entering your age, entering your weight (kg), entering your height (cm) and finally choosing your activity level from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Choose your sex from the list.
2. Enter your age.
3. Enter your weight (kg).
4. Enter your height (cm).
5. Choose your activity level from the list.
6. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.

## Formula

Mifflin-St Jeor BMR × activity factor. BMR = 10 × kg + 6.25 × cm − 5 × age + 5 (men) or − 161 (women).

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Calorie Calculator](/calorie-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A 30-year-old man, 75 kg and 178 cm, moderately active, burns about 2,700 kcal a day. Eating 2,200 would lose about 0.5 kg a week. Try the same figures in the [Calorie Calculator](/calorie-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Sex: Male, Age: 30, Weight: 75 kg, Height: 178 cm, Activity level: Moderate (3–5 days/week)), the [Calorie Calculator](/calorie-calculator) returns Maintenance calories: 2,662 kcal/day, Mild weight loss (−0.25 kg/wk): 2,412 kcal, Weight loss (−0.5 kg/wk): 2,162 kcal, Weight gain (+0.5 kg/wk): 3,162 kcal. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [BMI Calculator](/bmi-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- A 500 kcal daily deficit ≈ 0.5 kg loss per week.
- Don't go below about 1,200 (women) or 1,500 (men) without medical advice.
- Prioritise protein to preserve muscle.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### How accurate is this?

Mifflin-St Jeor is among the most accurate predictive equations, typically within about 10% for most people. For figures that matter, such as money, health or legal deadlines, check the result against an authoritative source before acting on it.

### What is TDEE?

Total Daily Energy Expenditure — your BMR plus calories burned through activity and digestion. Try it with your own numbers in the [Calorie Calculator](/calorie-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Calorie Calculator use?

Mifflin-St Jeor BMR × activity factor. BMR = 10 × kg + 6.25 × cm − 5 × age + 5 (men) or − 161 (women). You can see it in action in the [Calorie Calculator](/calorie-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Calorie Calculator?

Just Sex, Age, Weight, Height and Activity level. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.

### Is the Calorie Calculator free to use?

Yes. The Calorie Calculator is free to use as often as you like, with no sign-up. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [Calorie Calculator](/calorie-calculator) and start straight away.
